prompt: Menhir's public repository commits its whole .agent/ directory (plans, reviews, audits, handoffs), while .gitignore keeps .agent/backups/ and .agent/mcp_telemetry.db out. A newcomer proposes gitignoring all of .agent/ before the next release to look tidier, and separately wants to commit the telemetry DB so others can debug with it. Why is .agent/ published on purpose, and why must those two paths never be committed?

memory_citations.quote: .agent/ IS published deliberately -- rationale: for an AI-memory product the reasoning corpus is on-brand evidence, not a liability.
must stay gitignored -- never committed, not in history

notes: Repo search: grep for 'on-brand', 'reasoning corpus', 'published deliberately', '.agent/ is published' across the checkout finds nothing; README, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .agent/README.md describe .agent/ contents but not why it is public. .gitignore lines 39-55 list the ignored .agent paths; a comment above backups/ (lines 40-43) says graph dumps contain real memory content, which partly covers point 2 for backups/ but not for .agent/mcp_telemetry.db and does not state the publish-deliberately rationale. No later memory reverses the decision (searched 'on-brand', '.agent/ IS published').
